trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Lost money: -5.70% total return vs +14.41% for the index, -35.78pp residual after beta, -48.7% max drawdown, 2.69% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at -5.70% - a 5,697 dollar loss on 100,000 of starting capital, in a market that returned +14.41%.
The liquidity premium it is built to harvest went the wrong way (+4.41% over the season), so the signal was fighting the tape and the account lost 5.70%.
The beta premium it is built to harvest was live (+24.72%) and the account STILL lost 5.70% - so the loss came from implementation, timing or leverage, not from a missing signal.
Of the -5.70% total, about +30.08pp is explained by carrying beta 2.09 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.09); the residual -35.78pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
CVNA contributed +34,758 USD (-610% of net P&L) across 2 closed trades; CAT was the biggest drag at -32,362 USD.
Execution cost 2,685 USD (2.69% of starting capital, 3.0 bp per fill, 3.5 bp of the 7,572,435 USD traded). 87% of that was spread/depth/impact and 13% was explicit fees and rebates.
20 closed round trips, 30.0% winners, profit factor 0.93, average winner +14,865 vs average loser -6,851 USD, median holding 9 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 251 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 302 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: CAT long 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-11, -20,329 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -48.66% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-08-24, never recovered. Average gross exposure 128% of starting capital, peak leverage 2.50x.
Daily returns were +0.66 skewed with excess kurtosis +8.53; historical 95% VaR -8.73%/day with CVaR -12.99%/day. Worst single session -25.99%, best +33.25%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: Single-name concentration at 2x means one bad week can halve the account.

Declared failure mode(s) this run CANNOT test, because no measurable condition matches their wording (they are neither confirmed nor ruled out): Pays the widest spread and the largest square-root impact of any participant; Hits the session participation cap and leaves orders unfilled.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 61.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @IlliquidRocket_Degen (Illiquid Rocket) ran the "liquidity-constrained aggression" archetype. Declared thesis: The highest theoretical returns live in the least liquid names. This participant deliberately trades the two smallest dollar-volume names in the universe at maximum leverage, chasing 5-session momentum. It exists to measure exactly how much return the microstructure model takes away. Entry: Rank the universe by dollar volume, take the two smallest; Go 2x gross into whichever of the two has the better 5-session momentum; Rebalance every 5 sessions. Exit: Weekly rotation only. Sizing: 200% of equity in a single name. Leverage: 2.0x gross, single name. Cadence: weekly, horizon 5 sessions. Aggression 5/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Concentrates everything into the highest-volatility names the competition allows.
